before.title: 2014-2020 Grand Cherokee EcoDiesel High-Pressure Fuel Pump Recall (Z46 / 22V-406)
before.description: Certain 2014-2020 Jeep Grand Cherokee (WK) vehicles with the 3.0L diesel engine are included in safety recall Z46 / NHTSA 22V-406. The high-pressure fuel pump can fail prematurely and introduce internal debris into the fuel system, causing fuel starvation. FCA says occupants may notice a malfunction indicator lamp, a fuel leak, abnormal engine noise, or a change in drive quality; fuel starvation can cause an unexpected loss of motive power and increase crash risk. Recall inclusion is VIN-specific. The prior card incorrectly included 2021-2023 vehicles and treated an old pump number plus a retail injector set and filters as a universal repair.
before.solution: Check the VIN for open recall Z46 and schedule the free repair with an authorized Jeep dealer. FCA's procedure is condition-dependent: a vehicle delivered in good running condition receives the campaign HPFP and associated non-contaminated-system service, while a non-running vehicle is diagnosed for pump failure and, when contamination is confirmed, receives the pump, in-tank modules, filters, injectors, rails, high-pressure tubes, fuel-system cleaning, and other campaign items specified for that vehicle. If the vehicle stalls, loses power, leaks fuel, or will not restart, move it to a safe location, shut it off, and arrange a tow rather than continuing to run the engine. Do not buy a retail CP4 pump, injector set, or filter bundle before VIN eligibility and contamination status are established.
symptoms: Unexpected loss of motive power or stalling
Malfunction indicator lamp
Fuel leak
Abnormal engine noise
Change in drive quality or a non-running condition
affectedSystems: fuel tank and in-tank pump modules when contamination is confirmed
fuel filters and high-pressure fuel tubes
fuel injectors and fuel rails when contamination is confirmed

before.title: 2014-2016 Grand Cherokee EcoDiesel DEF/SCR Faults - Diagnose Before Replacing Parts
before.description: A DEF/SCR warning or reductant-system DTC on a 2014-2016 Grand Cherokee EcoDiesel does not prove that the complete DEF tank has failed. FCA documentation shows materially different causes and remedies within this model range: one defined 2015 population received PCM software and a fluid-level reset for reductant codes, while a separate, narrowly defined 2015 VIN/build population with manufacturing contamination required several DEF/SCR components. Eligible vehicles that received the Approved Emissions Modification may also have extended-warranty coverage for multiple DEF-system parts and diagnostic scanning. The previous card collapsed all of these paths into one integrated-tank diagnosis and published two unverified retail searches.
before.solution: Record the exact DTCs, freeze-frame data, warning text, VIN, build date, and current PCM software level. Have an EcoDiesel-capable shop or Jeep dealer follow the code-specific FCA diagnostic procedure and check whether a VIN-specific service action, applicable software update, or AEM extended warranty applies. Do not infer a failed tank from P20E8, P204F, P20EE, or another reductant code alone: verify the relevant pressure, heater, level/temperature input, fluid quality/contamination, delivery line, injector, SCR catalyst, wiring, and control-software path specified for that VIN. Replace only the component the tests and applicable FCA procedure identify. No retail part is published until the failed component and VIN fitment are confirmed.
symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp
Service DEF or reductant-system warning
A stored DEF/SCR pressure, heater, quality, or system-performance DTC
affectedSystems: DEF storage tank and level/temperature inputs
DEF supply module, pump, and delivery lines

before.title: 2014-2019 Grand Cherokee EcoDiesel EGR Cooler Fire-Risk Recall (W79 / 20V-699)
before.description: Certain 2014-2019 Jeep Grand Cherokee vehicles with the 3.0L EcoDiesel engine are included in safety recall W79 / NHTSA 20V-699. NHTSA lists 28,884 potentially involved Jeep vehicles. Thermal fatigue can cause the EGR cooler to crack internally over time, allowing pre-heated vaporized coolant into the EGR system; under some conditions the mixture can combust inside the intake manifold and lead to a vehicle fire. Recall inclusion is VIN-specific. The prior card overstated the Jeep population as 34,334, attached unsupported generic EGR codes, and offered OEM, aftermarket, manifold, and gasket purchases even though the recall repair is free and inspection-dependent.
before.solution: Check the VIN for open recall W79 and schedule the free repair with an authorized Jeep dealer. FCA's procedure replaces the EGR cooler using campaign parts. If the malfunction indicator lamp is illuminated, the dealer checks for P0299 and P2D2F; when either is present, the intake manifold is inspected and leak-tested and is replaced only if perforation is confirmed. Monitor the coolant level as FCA advises and contact the dealer if it is consistently low. If there is smoke, a burning smell, visible fire, or rapid coolant loss, stop safely, shut the engine off, move occupants away, and seek emergency/towing assistance. Do not buy an EGR cooler, manifold, aftermarket cooler, or gasket bundle in place of the VIN-specific recall remedy.
symptoms: Coolant level is consistently low
Malfunction indicator lamp may be illuminated
Evidence of intake-manifold damage when the FCA inspection criteria are met
affectedSystems: intake manifold when perforation is confirmed

FCA safety recall W79 service instructions: Diesel EGR Cooler
FCA W79 owner notification: Diesel EGR Cooler

communityRecommendations.content: Do not substitute an aftermarket EGR cooler for an open safety recall. Confirm W79 by VIN and use the free dealer remedy.
The intake manifold is not an automatic add-on. FCA calls for inspection and leak testing when P0299 or P2D2F is present, with replacement only if perforation is found.
The corrected Jeep population is 28,884 potentially involved vehicles; 34,334 was not the Jeep-only total in NHTSA's report.

before.title: 3.0L EcoDiesel Oil Cooler Failure Causing Oil/Coolant Cross-Contamination and Engine Damage
before.description: The integrated engine oil cooler/oil-filter housing on the 3.0L EcoDiesel develops internal failures that let engine oil and coolant cross-contaminate — owners report 'milkshake' oil and oil in the coolant bottle. Casting debris left in the engine can become trapped in the cooler and, with vibration, wear holes through the cooler's thin metal. If the leak isn't caught early it leads to overheating, coolant in the oil destroying bearings, and in many documented cases catastrophic engine failure requiring a long block — repairs that have run owners well into five figures. Failures are widely reported starting around 100k-140k miles.
before.solution: Replace the oil cooler/oil-filter housing assembly at the first sign of oil-coolant mixing; many EcoDiesel owners proactively fit an upgraded external oil cooler kit to eliminate the cross-contamination path. Flush the cooling and oil systems thoroughly after any contamination event, and inspect bearings/engine condition before returning to service. Address any coolant loss or emulsified oil immediately — continuing to drive risks a total-engine repair.
symptoms: Milky/emulsified 'milkshake' engine oil
Oil found in the coolant reservoir or coolant in the oil
Unexplained coolant loss
Engine overheating
Low oil pressure or knocking after contamination

citations.title: FCA TSB 09-003-19: GEN-2 and GEN-3 3.0L Oil Filter Cartridge Identification Differences

communityRecommendations.content: Do not buy an oil cooler from the old card. The reviewed FCA bulletin documents a filter-generation mismatch risk, not the old casting-debris and universal cross-contamination claim.
The linked filter is for the original 2014-2019 GEN-2 3.0L application. Never substitute the newer GEN-3 cap-and-element design because the cartridges look similar.

before.title: 2011-2013 Grand Cherokee 3.6L Low Oil Between Changes - Test Before Replacing PCV Parts
before.description: Low engine oil between changes on a 2011-2013 Grand Cherokee 3.6L does not by itself prove that the PCV valve or hose has failed. Chrysler's gasoline-engine diagnostic bulletin requires a formal oil-consumption test first. Only when the vehicle fails that test does the procedure move to checking the complete PCV system for restriction, the correct valve part, and the correct vacuum source; if the PCV system is correct, compression and cylinder leak-down testing follow. The previous card described the PCV system as the primary and most common cause, prescribed an unsupported 30,000-mile replacement interval, recommended a catch can, and attached P052E and P0300 without reviewed FCA support.
before.solution: Verify the oil was filled to the correct level and document mileage and oil added under Chrysler's oil-consumption test procedure. If the vehicle passes the test, do not replace PCV parts for this concern. If it fails, inspect the full PCV path for restriction, confirm the installed valve is the correct part for the VIN and engine, and verify the correct intake-vacuum source; repair only a fault found in those checks. If the PCV system is correct, record a cylinder-compression test and perform a leak-down test using the applicable service specifications. Also diagnose any visible external leak separately. Do not order a PCV valve, revised hose, or catch can from oil use alone, and do not treat P052E or P0300 as part of this card without an actual scan and code-specific diagnosis.
symptoms: Engine oil level drops between documented checks
Oil must be added before the scheduled oil change
The vehicle fails Chrysler's formal oil-consumption test
affectedSystems: piston rings, cylinders, and valve sealing when PCV checks pass

citations.title: Chrysler TSB 09-001-13: Gasoline Engine Diagnostic Inspection Procedure

communityRecommendations.content: Record the exact oil level, mileage, and quantity added. A repeatable consumption test is more useful than guessing from one low reading.
Do not treat the PCV valve as the default repair. Chrysler's sequence checks it only after a failed oil-consumption test and moves to compression and leak-down testing when PCV is correct.
The old 30,000-mile PCV interval, catch-can recommendation, P052E/P0300 mapping, and universal valve/hose purchases were removed because the reviewed FCA evidence does not support them for this card.

before.contentUpdateSummary: Narrowed the record to Chrysler's documented 2011-2013 diagnostic scope, replaced a presumed-PCV repair with the required consumption/PCV/compression/leak-down sequence, and removed six unsafe search links.

before.title: 2012-2021 Grand Cherokee 3.6L Oil Filter Adapter Leak - Identify the Source First
before.description: Oil found around the Pentastar oil filter adapter does not prove that the complete adapter or oil cooler has cracked. FCA's service guidance separates several repair paths: a cap O-ring that is cut, damaged, or installed in the wrong groove; five adapter bolts that are not at the specified torque; and a confirmed leak at the adapter-to-block O-rings and gaskets. FCA's 2021 guidance tells technicians to reseal a confirmed interface leak rather than replace the adapter on the covered non-2014 vehicles, while model-year 2014 is handled as an adapter-replacement exception. The previous card treated 2011-2020 vehicles alike, prescribed an aluminum assembly, implied oil/coolant cross-contamination, and listed P0128 and P26B7 without reviewed support.
before.solution: Clean the area and add approved oil dye so the source can be observed before parts are ordered. Inspect the oil-filter-cap O-ring for damage and confirm it is seated in the correct groove. Check the five oil-filter-adapter bolts against FCA's 12 N-m specification and document any under-torque condition. If dye confirms a leak at the adapter-to-block interface, follow the current VIN- and model-year-specific FCA service information: the cited guidance calls for O-ring/gasket kit 68191356A$ rather than a complete adapter on covered vehicles other than model year 2014, and calls for adapter replacement on model year 2014. Transfer sensors only when the applicable replacement procedure requires it. Verify the exact suffix and current part by VIN before ordering. Do not buy a housing, cooler, seal kit, or aluminum conversion until the leak source and installed housing are confirmed.
symptoms: Oil visible around the oil-filter cap or adapter
Oil collecting in the engine valley or running down the engine

before.title: 3.6L Pentastar Plastic Oil Filter Housing / Oil-Cooler Assembly Cracks Causing Oil and Coolant Leaks
before.description: The 3.6L Pentastar's oil filter housing is an integrated plastic oil-cooler assembly that mounts in the valley under the intake manifold. The plastic warps and becomes brittle from repeated heat cycling — expanding and contracting at a different rate than the aluminum engine — so the gaskets can no longer seal, and the housing can crack (even from over-tightening the oil filter cap). Because the assembly also routes engine coolant through its integrated oil cooler, failures produce oil leaks, coolant loss, and in worse cases oil-and-coolant intermixing. Owners typically first notice oil pooling in the valley/rear of the engine and/or unexplained low coolant. This is one of the most common Pentastar shop repairs; Chrysler discontinued the plastic assembly but never issued a recall. It is a different failure and location from the oil-pan-gasket/oil-pressure-sensor leak, and affects a wide 2011-2023 Pentastar population across WK2 and WL Grand Cherokees.
before.solution: Replace the failed oil filter housing/oil-cooler assembly. The durable accepted fix is an upgraded all-aluminum housing (e.g., Dorman 926-959, earlier 926-876) rather than the failure-prone plastic OE part, with new housing/cooler gaskets and O-rings and fresh oil/coolant. If oil-coolant intermixing occurred, flush the cooling system and change oil. Because the housing sits under the intake manifold, replacement includes intake removal, so shops often do the intake gasket, spark plugs, and a coolant flush at the same time. Housing-only labor+part runs roughly $400-$900, rising with the added items.
symptoms: Oil pooling at rear/valley/passenger side of engine
Burning oil smell from engine bay
Unexplained low coolant / coolant loss
Oil and coolant intermixing (milky oil or oily coolant) in severe cases
Visible oil residue around the oil filter cap/housing

before.title: 3.6L Pentastar Upgrade Rocker Arm / Intake Camshaft Lobe Wear Causing Misfire and Tick
before.description: The updated/'Upgrade' 3.6L Pentastar V6 (used on later WK2 and the WL fifth-gen) suffers premature wear of the intake rocker-arm roller bearings and/or intake camshaft lobes, traced by TSB to a manufacturing issue. As the rocker bearing or cam lobe wears, the valve no longer opens fully, producing a distinct ticking noise and a misfire on the affected cylinder; if ignored the failing rocker can damage the camshaft. This is a separate failure from the early-2011-2013 left-head defect and from the 5.7 HEMI MDS lifter — it affects the V6 valvetrain across both generations.
before.solution: Diagnose a cylinder-specific misfire accompanied by a valvetrain tick with a scope/inspection of the intake rocker arms and camshaft lobes. Replace worn rocker arms and, where the cam lobe is scored, the camshaft, per the applicable Pentastar Upgrade TSB; address promptly to avoid camshaft and follow-on damage. Replace spark plug/coil first only to rule out the easy cause — a persistent misfire with a tick is valvetrain, not ignition.
symptoms: Cylinder-specific misfire code
Ticking/tapping noise from the valvetrain
Rough idle, hesitation, check-engine light
Misfire that does not move when coil/plug is swapped
Reduced power

before.title: 1999-2004 4.0L Coolant Loss or Misfire — Confirm the Cylinder Head and Leak Path First
before.description: A cracked cylinder head or failed head gasket can produce coolant loss, overheating, rough running, or cylinder leakage on a 4.0L Grand Cherokee, but the previous card treated every 1999-2004 vehicle as if its installed casting and failure mode were already known. Heads may have been replaced during the vehicle's life, and DaimlerChrysler also documented P0300 and single-cylinder misfires from slow-closing exhaust valves caused by carbon. A model year, a P030x code, or coolant loss by itself does not prove a crack between cylinders 3 and 4 or identify the correct replacement head.
before.solution: Start with the cooling system and the actual failure path: pressure-test the system cold, inspect external leak points, test for combustion gas where appropriate, and inspect the oil and coolant for cross-contamination. For a misfire, follow the factory diagnostic path and use compression and leak-down results rather than assigning the code to the head. Record the installed casting/foundry markings because a prior repair may have changed the head. If removal is justified, have the head and deck inspected and pressure-tested by a qualified machine shop. Only after the crack, deck condition, installed casting, and required machining are known should the shop select an application-specific head, gasket set, and fastener plan. No universal replacement head is linked here.

Overheating or unstable coolant temperature
Rough running or a cylinder-specific misfire
Combustion gas in the cooling system
Oil and coolant cross-contamination

before.description: The 4.0L inline-six routes oil through an aluminum oil-filter adapter housing bolted to the block; its O-rings harden and leak with age, dripping oil down the rear/side of the block. Confirm the source with the housing area cleaned and dye if needed before condemning the rear main.

Because the oil migrates rearward, it is very commonly misdiagnosed as a rear main seal or oil-pan leak. One of the most frequent 4.0L oil-leak searches for ZJ/WJ owners.
proposal.solution: Replace the oil-filter adapter O-ring kit — Crown Automotive / Mopar 4720363 (a 3-O-ring kit, adapter retained by a T60 Torx bolt). Clean the mating surface first. A popular permanent alternative deletes the adapter housing and runs a shorter PH3614-style filter directly. Confirm the source with the housing area cleaned and dye if needed before condemning the rear main.
symptoms: Oil leak/drip on the passenger side and rear of the block
Oil smell and spots under the vehicle
Oil on the oil filter and adapter area
Gradual oil-level drop with no smoke

citations.title: 1999 Jeep Grand Cherokee 4.0L Service Manual: Engine Lubrication and Oil Filter Adapter

communityRecommendations.content: Degrease the area and establish the first wet point before buying parts. Oil from the filter gasket, sender, valve-cover edge, oil-pan rail, or rear of the engine can cross the same area.
The old card's T60-fastener and adapter-delete advice was not universal enough for this full year span. Follow the service information for the exact adapter installed on the vehicle.

before.title: 4.7L V8 Crankshaft Position Sensor Failure Causing Hot-Restart No-Start and Random Stalling
before.description: The crankshaft position sensor (CKP) on the 4.7L (and 4.0L) Grand Cherokee commonly fails from heat-soak: it works when cold but its internal resistance rises when hot, so the PCM loses the crank signal and the engine won't restart until it cools 30-60 minutes, or it stalls randomly while driving. A cranks-but-no-start after a hot soak is the classic signature and a top WJ search.
before.solution: Verify with a scan tool (loss of CKP signal / no RPM during crank) rather than parts-swapping. Replace with a quality sensor — Mopar crankshaft position sensor 56028666AB fits 1999-2004 4.7L (56028133-series is the CAMSHAFT sensor, do not confuse). Use OEM Mopar or premium NGK/NTK; cheap sensors frequently fail again. On some 4.7L applications the starter must be removed for access.
symptoms: Cranks but will not start when hot; restarts after cooling down
Random stalling while driving with immediate/eventual restart
Intermittent no-crank-signal
Tachometer drops to zero while stalling

citations.title: 2004 Jeep Grand Cherokee 4.7L Service Manual: P0320 Diagnostic

NHTSA 04V-112: 2004 Grand Cherokee 4.0L CKP Recall Population

communityRecommendations.content: Do not replace the sensor from P0320 alone. The factory tree also lists CKP supply, ground, signal wiring, cam signal, and PCM causes.
Recall 04V-112 is a limited 2004 4.0L campaign; it does not make a 1999-2004 4.7L sensor replacement a recall repair.
The 4.7L sensor sits above the starter. Follow the factory O-ring, flush-seating, and torque precautions so the new sensor is not damaged during installation.

before.title: 2004 545RFE Intermittent Low-Line-Pressure or Gear-Ratio DTCs — Check TCM Build Date
before.description: DaimlerChrysler TSB 08-016-05 describes an internal TCM circuit fault that may cause an intermittent low-line-pressure or gear-ratio DTC and limp-in on a specific 2004 WJ/WG Grand Cherokee population. The vehicle must have the 545RFE (sales code DGQ), a 4.7L or 4.7L High Output engine, and fall within the bulletin's April 7, 2004 through February 27, 2005 vehicle build range. Suspect TCMs have date codes 0984 through 0405. This is not a universal 1999-2010 transmission-overheating/shudder diagnosis, and it does not justify buying filters, fluid, a cooler, valve-body kits, or a solenoid pack from the symptom alone.
before.solution: Confirm the VIN build record, 545RFE sales code DGQ, stored transmission DTCs, and TCM event data. Read digits three through six of the TCM barcode; TSB 08-016-05 identifies 0984 through 0405 as the suspect controller build range. If the vehicle or controller date is outside scope, the bulletin does not apply and the transmission complaint needs its normal diagnostic path. For an in-scope vehicle, use the bulletin's P0868/gear-ratio decision path and compare desired, scan-reported actual, and mechanically measured line pressure with correct fluid level and temperature. Inspect wiring, connectors, cooler lines, leaks, and engine driveability first. The repair may involve the TCM and, when low pressure was present, inspection for clutch-disc damage; it is not a universal retail-parts fix. No commerce links are shown until those findings identify the required repair.

Malfunction indicator lamp with a low-line-pressure or gear-ratio fault

P0731-P0736 or P1736 gear-ratio fault

before.title: 2023-2025 Grand Cherokee 4xe Engine Sand-Contamination Recall (78C / 25V-766)
before.description: Certain 2023-2025 Jeep Grand Cherokee 4xe vehicles are included in FCA safety recall 78C / NHTSA 25V-766. FCA's amended report lists 39,975 potentially involved Grand Cherokee PHEVs built from July 19, 2023 through April 10, 2025. Sand left from the engine-block casting process can contaminate internal components and lead to catastrophic engine failure, an engine-compartment fire, or an unexpected and unrecoverable loss of propulsion. FCA says a knocking noise from the engine compartment and/or a malfunction indicator lamp may occur before failure, but recall inclusion is VIN-specific.
before.solution: Check the VIN for open recall 78C and contact an authorized Jeep dealer. FCA's current remedy reprograms the Powertrain Control Module with software that detects and monitors for potential pending engine-bearing failure. If the software confirms bearing failure, FCA replaces the long block or engine. FCA's March 2026 report also identifies warranty extension XC2 with unlimited years and unlimited mileage for impacted customers who receive defect-related messaging and need a long block or engine. Follow the official do-not-drive and park-outside advisories until the VIN-specific remedy is completed; if knocking, a malfunction light, smoke, fire, or loss of propulsion occurs, stop safely, move occupants away, and arrange dealer/towing or emergency assistance as appropriate. Do not self-source an engine for a free safety-recall repair.
symptoms: Knocking noise from the engine compartment
Malfunction indicator lamp
Unexpected loss of propulsion
Engine-compartment smoke or fire
affectedSystems: engine block and internal engine bearings

before.title: 2022-2026 Grand Cherokee 4xe High-Voltage Battery Fire-Risk Recall (68C / 25V-741)
before.description: Certain 2022-2026 Jeep Grand Cherokee 4xe vehicles are included in FCA safety recall 68C / NHTSA 25V-741. FCA's amended report lists 91,847 potentially involved Grand Cherokee PHEVs built from July 23, 2021 through November 25, 2025. In rare circumstances, cells in the high-voltage battery pack may have separator damage which, combined with other internal cell interactions, can lead to a vehicle fire while parked or driving. FCA identifies no warning before the condition. The prior card used the wrong recall number and offered a complete traction-battery purchase even though the remedy is a free VIN-specific campaign.
before.solution: Check the VIN for open recall 68C and contact an authorized Jeep dealer. Until the recall remedy is completed, follow FCA and NHTSA's instruction not to recharge the vehicle and to park it outside, away from structures and other vehicles. FCA's remedy is a software flash followed by high-voltage battery replacement if needed; the amended report also provides an unlimited-years/unlimited-mileage warranty extension for impacted customers who receive defect-related messaging and need a battery. Vehicles previously repaired under superseded recall 95B / 24V-720 still need the new 68C remedy if the VIN is included. If smoke, heat, a burning smell, or fire is observed, move away from the vehicle and call emergency services. Do not buy or install a salvage or retail high-voltage pack in place of the recall.
symptoms: FCA identifies no advance warning before the battery condition
Smoke, heat, or fire from the high-voltage battery area

before.title: 5.7L HEMI Exhaust Manifold Bolt/Stud Failure Causing Exhaust Tick and Leak
before.description: On 5.7L HEMI-equipped Grand Cherokees, the steel bolts/studs that hold the cast-iron exhaust manifolds to the cylinder heads repeatedly heat-cycle and snap, most commonly at the rear of each manifold. The broken hardware opens a small gap that lets exhaust escape, producing a metallic 'tick' or 'tap' that is loudest on a cold start and quiets as the engine warms and the metal expands to temporarily reseal the leak. This is a well-known HEMI-wide failure (shared with Durango and Ram 1500) and is distinct from the MDS lifter 'HEMI tick.' Left unrepaired it worsens, can fail an emissions/exhaust inspection, and the broken stud ends can seize in the head and require drilling/extraction.
before.solution: Replace the failed manifold bolts/studs with the updated Mopar double-ended stud hardware and new exhaust manifold gaskets; many shops convert all fasteners to studs/nuts so the manifold can be torqued evenly. Use new hardware on every bolt location — heat-fatigued originals will fail again. Confirm the diagnosis by listening for a cold-start tick that fades when warm and inspecting for soot/leak tracks at the manifold-to-head flange. If a stud has broken flush, it must be drilled and extracted; in severe cases a warped manifold is resurfaced or replaced.
symptoms: Metallic ticking or tapping noise loudest on cold start
Tick quiets or disappears as engine warms up
Exhaust/ticking noise from the engine bay under acceleration
Soot or black leak marks at the manifold-to-cylinder-head joint
Slight exhaust smell at idle

citations.title: FCA TSB 09-019-23: Cold Engine Ticking Noise From Exhaust Manifold Area

communityRecommendations.content: Do not order a manifold kit from the word 'tick' alone. FCA's procedure requires the cold-noise source and an actual manifold crack to be confirmed first.
Use every component in the updated kit. FCA specifically calls for the supplied gasket, new fasteners, heat shield, and tie bar, including the shorter 06510140AA fastener at the right-front position.

fixParts.note: FCA TSB 09-019-23 identifies 68591586AA as the left-side kit for WK/WD/WL. The exact linked item is a new genuine Mopar listing. Confirm the vehicle has a covered 5.7L engine, confirm the left manifold is cracked, and verify that the sealed package contains the complete current kit before purchase.

before.title: 2011-2021 Quadra-Lift Warning or Uneven Ride Height - Diagnose Before Parts
before.description: Quadra-Lift is a closed, electronically controlled air-suspension system, so a Service Air Suspension message, a low corner, or a denied height change does not identify one universal failed part. The factory diagnostic path covers electrical and communication faults, fuses and voltage, pinched or damaged lines, leaking springs, disconnected sensor linkages, water or blockage in the compressor intake, air-mass loss, valve/compressor faults, software, and the Air Suspension Control Module. The prior card also incorrectly treated SRT and Trackhawk as automatic Quadra-Lift applications; applicability should be established by sales code SER or the vehicle build sheet.
before.solution: Confirm the vehicle is equipped with Quadra-Lift sales code SER, record the exact ASCM DTCs and environmental data, and check VIN/build-date-specific FCA bulletins before ordering hardware. Follow the factory sequence: repair voltage or communication faults first; inspect fuses, air lines, springs, height-sensor linkages, compressor intake/filter, and visible plumbing; then use a capable scan tool to run the Air Mass and Air Ride Height routines and follow the DTC-specific tree. On 2011-2012 vehicles built before May 1, 2012, U0415-00 or C159E-15 with a Service Air Suspension message may be addressed by FCA TSB 08-034-12's ASCM software update. Replace only the component proven failed. A completely depleted system requires the specified refill equipment, scan-tool procedure, and purity-class-5 nitrogen; do not fill it with ordinary shop air or shotgun-replace springs, sensors, and the compressor.
symptoms: Service Air Suspension message
One corner or one axle sits low
Ride-height change is slow, denied, or inoperative
Quadra-Lift height indicators flash or normal leveling is disabled
affectedSystems: compressor, dryer, valve block, and reservoir
Air Suspension Control Module and software

before.title: 1999-2010 Airbag Light Plus Horn or Wheel-Control Faults - Scan SRS First
before.description: The clockspring is a plausible shared point when a Grand Cherokee has an airbag warning together with a failed horn, cruise control, or steering-wheel buttons. Factory wiring confirms that those circuits pass through the clockspring/steering-control assembly. That symptom combination does not prove the clockspring has failed, however: an SRS indicator means the restraint controller detected a monitored fault, and horn switches, relays, wiring, connectors, steering-control electronics, airbag circuits, and controller faults require separate diagnosis. The old card also combined 1999-2004 WJ and 2005-2010 WK part numbers without complete catalog or configuration proof.
before.solution: Treat an illuminated airbag indicator as a safety fault and have the SRS scanned with a restraint-capable tool. Record the exact active and stored DTCs, follow the model-year circuit tree, and test the horn and steering-wheel functions independently before condemning the clockspring. If circuit testing confirms the clockspring/steering-control assembly, select the replacement by VIN, model year, steering-wheel controls, steering-angle-sensor configuration, and current Mopar supersession. The assembly must be centered and the steering wheel kept in the correct position. SRS service can cause accidental deployment: follow the factory disable procedure, isolate the negative battery cable, wait the specified discharge time, and use trained service if you are not qualified. After repair, clear and recheck SRS DTCs and verify every wheel function.
symptoms: Airbag or SRS warning indicator
Horn inoperative from the steering wheel
Cruise-control or steering-wheel buttons inoperative
Fault changes with steering-wheel position

communityRecommendations.content: Do not probe airbag inflator circuits with an ordinary test light or meter and do not rotate an uncentered replacement clockspring. Follow the model-year SRS procedure or use a qualified technician.
Save the exact SRS DTCs before clearing them. The lamp plus a dead horn is a useful clue, but the DTC and circuit test determine whether the clockspring is actually open.

before.title: 2012-2014 Alternator-Diode Safety Recalls (P60 / T36)
before.description: Certain 2012-2014 Jeep Grand Cherokee vehicles are covered by alternator-diode safety recalls P60 / NHTSA 14V-634 or T36 / NHTSA 17V-435. P60 covers specified 3.6L vehicles with a 160A alternator. T36 covers VIN-included WK vehicles with electro-hydraulic power steering and specified 3.6L or 5.7L, 160A, 180A, or 220A configurations. FCA says thermal or rapid diode failure can stop alternator output, cause a stall with limited warning, or create a resistive short that produces heat, smoke, or an underhood fire. The exact campaign and completion status are VIN-specific.
before.solution: Check the VIN for open P60 / 14V-634 and T36 / 17V-435 campaigns and schedule an authorized Jeep dealer if either is incomplete. FCA's T36 procedure has the dealer inspect the alternator part-number tag; a listed improved unit needs no further action, while a suspect, illegible, missing, aftermarket, or remanufactured unit is replaced under the campaign with an alternator containing improved diodes. The recall repair is free for an eligible VIN, and the owner notices include a reimbursement path for qualifying prior repairs. Do not use the old retail alternator, battery, starter, charger, or EV-charger links in place of the recall. If the vehicle loses electrical power, stalls, or shows alternator heat, smoke, or fire, stop safely, move occupants away, and arrange towing or emergency assistance as appropriate.
symptoms: Limited or no warning before alternator output is lost
Battery or charging-system warning
Electrical systems lose power or the engine stalls
Heat, smoke, burning odor, or fire from the alternator area
affectedSystems: vehicle electrical power and engine operation

before.title: 2014-2018 Uconnect Reboots, Accessory Faults or Battery Drain - Separate the Causes
before.description: Uconnect resets or a blank screen, intermittent accessories, a discharged battery, and communication faults may occur together, but they do not establish that the Body Control Module is defective. Radio software or hardware, a weak battery or charging problem, poor power or ground, damaged CAN wiring or terminals, another module that will not sleep, and a true internal module fault can overlap. FCA has a software bulletin for specific early 2014 WK vehicles with RA3/RA4 radios, including radio resets and radio-caused battery drain, but that bulletin is sales-code and build-date specific and does not justify replacing a BCM, Intelligent Battery Sensor, or battery on every 2014-2018 vehicle.
before.solution: Start with a complete vehicle scan and save active, stored, and environmental data before clearing anything. Load-test the battery, verify charging voltage, and repair low-voltage faults first. Inspect the relevant fuses, power feeds, grounds, connectors, and CAN wiring, then measure key-off draw only after the vehicle has completed its normal sleep period and isolate the circuit that remains awake. For radio resets, identify the exact radio sales code and vehicle build date and check the VIN for the applicable FCA software or radio procedure. For a lost-communication fault, determine whether the named module is actually offline, whether multiple modules logged against it, and whether its power, ground, and network circuits pass before condemning it. Replace and VIN-configure a BCM, radio, IBS, or battery only when the component-specific test proves it failed.
symptoms: Uconnect radio resets, locks up, goes blank, or responds slowly
Intermittent accessory or warning-lamp behavior
Battery is discharged after the vehicle sits
One or more modules store lost-communication faults
affectedSystems: body power, grounds, fuses, and CAN wiring

communityRecommendations.content: U0140 means communication with the BCM was lost; it does not prove the BCM itself failed. Voltage, power, ground, wiring, network, and reporting-module faults must be separated first.
Ask the shop to show the sleep-current measurement, the circuit that stayed awake, and the network scan before authorizing an expensive programmed module.

before.title: Body/Unibody Rust-Through — Rocker Panels, Rear Wheel Arches and Floor Pans
before.description: ZJ (1993-1998) and especially WJ (1999-2004) Grand Cherokees in salt/rust-belt climates are notorious for corrosion of the rocker panels, rear quarter/wheel-arch lips, floor pans and rear cargo area. Because these are unibody structures, the rot is both cosmetic and structural, and it is a very common reason high-mileage examples fail inspection or get retired.
before.solution: Cut out corroded metal and weld in replacement panels: aftermarket rockers (Key Parts 0484-101 driver / 0484-102 passenger for 99-04 WJ) and rear wheel arches (Key Parts 0484-147), plus floor-pan sections as needed (Mill Supply / Classic 2 Current). Requires welding — professional bodywork recommended. Undercoat afterward and keep the rocker/pinchweld drain holes clear to slow recurrence.
symptoms: Bubbling paint and rust-through on rockers and rear wheel-arch lips
Perforated floor pans / water in cabin
Flaking rust in the rear cargo/spare-tire area
Structural weakness at jack points

before.title: A/C Condenser Refrigerant Leak Causing Warm Air and Compressor Cut-Out
before.description: Because the A/C condenser sits at the very front of the Grand Cherokee behind the grille, it is highly exposed to rocks and road debris, which puncture the thin tubes and cause refrigerant loss. Condenser leaks are one of the leading causes of an A/C that blows lukewarm or no cold air; as refrigerant escapes, the system's pressure sensor will eventually disable the compressor to protect it. Owners commonly chase recharges that don't hold before the leaking condenser is identified.
before.solution: Perform a dye or electronic leak test to confirm the condenser as the leak point. A leaking condenser cannot be repaired and must be replaced, followed by an evacuation, vacuum, and recharge with the correct refrigerant/oil. Replace the receiver/drier as part of the job. Address any debris damage to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: A/C blows warm or only slightly cool air
Cooling that works briefly then fades (slow leak)
Compressor not engaging due to low-pressure lockout
Refrigerant recharge that doesn't last
Visible oily residue/dye at the condenser

before.title: Capless Fuel Filler Neck Failure Causing Pump Repeatedly Clicking Off / Won't Accept Fuel (WK2)
before.description: WK2 Grand Cherokees use a capless (Easy Fuel) filler neck with a spring-loaded flapper door and an internal one-way check valve. Over time the flapper mechanism sticks or fails to seal, and the check valve at the tank inlet can hang up, causing the fuel pump nozzle to click off repeatedly and refuse to fill the tank — the classic 'won't take gas' complaint, often worse with modern ORVR pump nozzles. FCA revised the filler-neck part number multiple times, indicating a recognized design weakness. Beyond the fueling nuisance, a poorly sealing filler can contribute to EVAP (P0455/P0456) complaints.
before.solution: Inspect the capless filler neck flapper and internal check valve; clean debris and verify the flapper closes/seals. If it sticks or the nozzle keeps clicking off, replace the capless fuel filler neck with the latest revised part. As a temporary field workaround owners report inserting the nozzle more slowly (or gently holding the flapper open) — but the durable fix is filler-neck replacement. Rule out a plugged EVAP/vent restriction if fill problems persist after replacement.
symptoms: Fuel pump nozzle clicks off after a few seconds
Tank very slow to fill or won't accept fuel
Fuel splashback at the filler
Broken or stuck flapper door in the filler
Occasional EVAP check-engine light (P0455/P0456)
Must trickle-fill to top off the tank

citations.title: FCA TSB 14-005-23: Fuel Nozzle Premature Shut Off

communityRecommendations.content: Do not order by the symptom alone. FCA requires the other hard-to-fill diagnostics first, and the correct tube changes with engine sales code and model year.

before.title: 2018 Trackhawk P0420/P0430 - Apply TSB 18-001-26 Before Buying Parts
before.description: FCA TSB 18-001-26 covers a 2018 WK Grand Cherokee equipped with the 6.2L supercharged ESD engine and 8HP95 DFS transmission when P0420 and/or P0430 is stored. A customer may also report reduced engine power associated with catalyst damage and restricted exhaust flow. The bulletin identifies PCM software as the cause addressed by its repair procedure. It does not apply to the 3.6L Pentastar population in the old card and does not name an upstream or downstream oxygen sensor as the repair.
before.solution: Confirm the vehicle is a covered 2018 WK with engine sales code ESD and transmission sales code DFS, save the DTC and freeze-frame information, and check the VIN and current calibration level. Follow FCA TSB 18-001-26: maintain the specified battery voltage, reprogram the PCM with the latest software using wiTECH or equivalent, and clear DTCs set during programming. If P0420/P0430 returns, exhaust restriction or loss of power remains, or other DTCs are present, continue with the current factory catalyst, fuel-control, misfire, exhaust-leak, and sensor diagnostics for the exact vehicle. Do not buy oxygen sensors or catalytic converters from the code alone.
symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp with P0420 and/or P0430
Possible reduced engine power if catalyst damage has restricted exhaust flow

before.title: 2011-2021 WK2 Rear Cargo Water Intrusion - Locate the Entry Path First
before.description: Water found in a WK2 Grand Cherokee cargo well, under the cargo floor, or near a rear pillar is a symptom, not proof that one grommet, weatherstrip, lamp gasket, antenna seal, or roof seam has failed. The factory water-leak procedure warns that water can travel through body cavities and appear far from the true entry point. The old card's shopping list could therefore send an owner to four unrelated products before the leak location was established.
before.solution: Dry the accessible area enough to see a new water track, protect affected electrical connectors and modules, and reproduce the conditions under which the leak occurs. Follow the factory water-leak procedure: visually inspect plugs, drains, alignment, seams, seals, and grommets; test one region at a time with an appropriate low-pressure stream or fan spray; remove trim only as needed for safe visual access; and trace the highest fresh water track to its actual entry point. Repair, reseat, or replace only the confirmed failed seal, seam, fastener, drain, weatherstrip, glass bond, lamp seal, or wiring pass-through using the current factory procedure and specified material. Dry wet insulation, inspect exposed terminals for corrosion, and repeat the water test before closing the trim. Do not smear generic RTV across several unconfirmed paths.
symptoms: Standing water or dampness in the rear cargo area
Wet cargo carpet or insulation after rain or washing
Water track near a rear pillar, liftgate opening, or cargo trim
Musty odor or interior condensation
affectedSystems: rear wiring and connectors if exposed to water

citations.title: 2012 Jeep Grand Cherokee Factory Service Manual: Water Leaks

communityRecommendations.content: The puddle location may not be the entry location. Do not buy a grommet, weatherstrip, sealant, or lamp seal until a controlled water test identifies the source.
Photograph the first fresh water track during the test and retest after the repair before reinstalling all wet trim and insulation.

before.title: Dual-Pane Panoramic Sunroof Water Leak Into Headliner/Pillars (TSB 23-102-23, WL 2021-2023)
before.description: On 5th-gen WL Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L with the dual-pane panoramic sunroof, water can leak into the headliner and A-pillar areas. Chrysler issued TSB 23-102-23 for 2021-2023 units built on or before Feb 6, 2023, identifying the wind deflector assembly as a cause: it can trap the sunroof panel and create a poor seal. Clogged front/rear sunroof drain channels are a second common cause, allowing water to seep into the headliner and pillars and potentially reach electrical components. A related TSB (23-035-21) addresses sunroof rattle from loose mounting fasteners on early 2021 builds.
before.solution: Per TSB 23-102-23, have the dealer replace the wind deflector assembly with the updated part. Independently, clear the front and rear sunroof drain tubes of debris to restore drainage. For sunroof rattle on early builds, TSB 23-035-21 replaces the sunroof mounting fasteners. Address leaks promptly to avoid wet headliner, mold, and corrosion of nearby electrical connectors.
symptoms: water dripping from headliner or A-pillar
wet headliner/carpet after rain or car wash
musty smell
sunroof rattle on rough roads

before.title: Early 3.6L Pentastar Left Cylinder Head Failure — Overheated Valve Seat Causing Ticking, Misfire and Check Engine Light (Warranty Extension X56)
before.description: On early 3.6L Pentastar V6 engines, the LEFT cylinder head (cylinders 2-4-6) is prone to premature failure. Premature wear of the exhaust valve seats and guides (attributed to improper material/hardening) causes valve-seat recession, producing a tell-tale tick, misfires on the left bank and an illuminated check-engine light. Chrysler acknowledged the condition in TSB 09-002-14 and issued warranty extension X56 covering the left cylinder head for 10 years / 150,000 miles (per warranty bulletin D-14-12, June 2014); it was never a safety recall. A production fix (hardened valve guides/seats, revised left head casting, reman part RL141353AC / updated OEM casting) was phased in during summer 2012 (heads stamped 2062 = 206th day of 2012 or later are the fixed version), so the highest-risk population is 2011-2012 builds plus early-2012-build 2013 units. before.title: ETC Warning or Limp Mode - Read the DTC Before Buying a Throttle Body
before.description: The electronic-throttle-control warning lamp and reduced-power or limp mode are protective responses, not a diagnosis that the throttle body has failed. Depending on the stored DTC and application, the factory path may lead to a stuck or contaminated throttle plate, throttle motor or position-sensor response, accelerator-pedal sensors, a five-volt supply fault, damaged wiring or terminals, or a PCM issue. The old card's thermostat shopping claim is not part of the cited ETC diagnostic path, and a throttle body should not be ordered from the warning lamp alone.
before.solution: Before clearing anything, record every PCM DTC, pending code, freeze-frame value, battery voltage, temperature, and the exact conditions under which reduced power occurred. Diagnose prerequisite five-volt-supply, throttle-position, accelerator-pedal, or other active faults in the order specified by the current factory procedure for that VIN and engine. For a P2111-style fault, inspect the throttle plate for binding or foreign material and run the scan-tool throttle-follower test, then test the motor circuits, connector terminals, and wiring as directed. For a pedal-correlation code such as P2138, follow the accelerator-pedal sensor and circuit procedure instead. Replace and relearn a throttle body only when the applicable test condemns it; do not buy a thermostat as an ETC rule-out part.
symptoms: Electronic throttle control warning lamp
Reduced engine output, limited RPM, or limp mode
Poor or absent accelerator response
One or more throttle, pedal, voltage-supply, or actuator DTCs
affectedSystems: throttle body motor and position sensors
PCM wiring, connectors, and voltage supplies

before.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump (ESIM/NVLD) Failure Triggers P0455/P0456 — Often Misdiagnosed as Gas Cap
before.description: The Jeep Grand Cherokee uses a Natural Vacuum Leak Detection (NVLD) approach for its EVAP system, implemented through the Evaporative System Integrity Module (ESIM) — commonly called the leak detection pump. The ESIM is a standalone unit (typically mounted on the charcoal canister near the rear driver-side wheel well) that seals the fresh-air vent and uses natural temperature-induced pressure changes to verify the fuel-vapor system holds vacuum. The internal seal/diaphragm and check mechanism in the ESIM are a well-documented common failure point on Chrysler/Jeep platforms. When the unit fails, the PCM cannot complete its EVAP self-test and falsely reports an EVAP leak, illuminating the check engine light even though no actual leak exists. Because the same codes are thrown by a loose or worn gas cap, the failure is frequently misdiagnosed: owners (and even shops) replace the gas cap first, the light returns, and the actual ESIM/leak-detection-pump fault is missed. A simple field test is to remove the ESIM and shake it — a rattle indicates the internal valve has come loose and the unit needs replacement. Note that the EVAP purge-valve hose on top of the engine also becomes brittle and cracks (covered by Jeep TSBs #25-002-15 REV-B and #18-035-20), producing the same codes, so the hose should be inspected before condemning the ESIM. This is an emissions-only fault: it does not harm the engine or transmission but will fail a state emissions/smog test.
before.solution: Diagnose before replacing parts. (1) Inspect/re-tighten or replace the gas cap and confirm it clicks and seals — rule out the cheapest cause first. (2) Visually inspect the thin plastic EVAP purge-valve hose on top of the engine for cracks/splits (especially at connection points) per TSB #25-002-15 REV-B; replace if brittle/cracked — this alone fixes many cases. (3) Locate the ESIM/leak detection pump (on the charcoal canister near the rear driver-side wheel well); remove and shake it — if it rattles, the internal valve has failed and the module must be replaced. Replacement is a straightforward DIY: a new ESIM (OEM, or aftermarket such as Dorman 310-219) installs in place of the old one. After replacement, clear the codes and complete a few drive/fill cycles to confirm the EVAP monitor passes and the light stays off. If codes persist after ESIM and hose service, smoke-test the EVAP system to find a remaining leak (canister, lines, or fuel-tank-side seals).
symptoms: Check engine light on (often intermittent, may clear and return)
OBD-II scan shows P0456 (small EVAP leak), P0455 (large EVAP leak), or P0457 (loose fuel cap / large leak)
"Check Fuel Cap" / gas cap warning message
Fuel/gasoline odor near the vehicle in some cases
Failed state emissions or smog test
Light returns shortly after a gas cap replacement (sign of misdiagnosis)
Occasional slightly extended cranking
ESIM rattles when removed and shaken (failed internal valve)

before.title: Front Blower Motor Resistor Failure — HVAC Fan Works Only on High Speed
before.description: The HVAC blower-motor resistor on ZJ (1993-1998) and WJ (1999-2004) Grand Cherokees commonly burns out, leaving the fan working only on the highest setting (which bypasses the resistor). A worn blower motor drawing excess amperage cooks the resistor, and the connector often overheats. Very common, cheap, high-search fix.
before.solution: Replace the blower motor resistor located under the passenger-side dash — Mopar 5012699AA (RU-358) fits 1999-2004 WJ with ATC; use the matching resistor for manual A/C (Crown 4720278 for 93-99 ZJ/WJ manual). If a new resistor fails quickly, also replace the aging blower motor and the burnt resistor connector/pigtail to stop repeat failures.
symptoms: Blower only runs on the highest (or a single) speed
No airflow on low/medium settings
Intermittent fan operation
Burnt smell or melted resistor connector

before.title: 2011-2021 WK2 Front-End Clunk - Isolate the Failed Joint, Link, Bushing, or Mount
before.description: A WK2 front-end clunk over bumps, during braking, or while steering can come from more than the sway-bar links or lower control arms named in the old card. The source can vary with loading and may involve a stabilizer link or bushing, control-arm bushing, ball joint, tie-rod end, shock or upper mount, wheel bearing, loose fastener, brake hardware, or another nearby component. Standard and high-performance suspension packages also use different side-specific parts. Ordering four components from the noise alone risks replacing good parts while leaving a safety-relevant loose joint in service.
before.solution: Record when the noise occurs and reproduce it safely on a controlled road test. With the vehicle supported according to the factory procedure, inspect wheel and tire security, brake hardware, steering linkage, stabilizer links and bushings, control-arm bushings, upper and lower ball joints, shocks and mounts, wheel bearings, subframe attachment, and nearby shields or loose hardware. Check joints and bushings in the loaded and unloaded positions specified by the service manual, and use chassis ears or controlled isolation when visual play is not obvious. If steering looseness, wheel movement, instability, or a damaged joint is present, stop driving until repaired. Replace only the confirmed failed component using the VIN, side, suspension sales code, and current supersession; torque at the specified ride-height condition and perform an alignment when the repair procedure requires it.
symptoms: Clunk or knock from the front over bumps
Noise during braking, acceleration, or steering load changes
Possible looseness, uneven tire wear, or steering change if a joint or bushing is worn

wheel hubs and nearby brake hardware

before.title: Front/Rear Differential Pinion Seal Leak and Gear Whine (WK2 4x4)
before.description: Grand Cherokee 4x4 differentials (and the transfer case) are a known spot for pinion-seal leaks — owners find gear oil weeping where the driveshaft meets the diff, leaving puddles and, if ignored, running the diff low on lube. A low/contaminated differential then produces a speed-related whine or howl (rising on acceleration or deceleration depending on which gear/bearing is loaded). RepairPal documents many pinion-seal/transfer-case leak cases on the platform. A caution: careless seal replacement (over-torquing the pinion nut and crushing the collapsible spacer) destroys pinion-bearing preload, so the repair must be done correctly.
before.solution: Inspect the front and rear diff pinion flanges and transfer-case output for gear-oil weepage; confirm fluid level. Replace the leaking pinion seal, marking pinion-nut position/turns to preserve preload (or setting new preload with a fresh crush sleeve) to avoid bearing damage. If gear whine is already present from prior low-lube running, evaluate the ring/pinion and bearings and refill with the correct spec gear oil. Address any transfer-case seal leaks at the same time.
symptoms: Gear-oil puddle/residue at the driveshaft-to-differential joint
Speed-dependent whine or howl from front or rear axle
Whine changes on acceleration vs deceleration
Low differential fluid level
Metal glitter on the diff fill plug (advanced wear)
Transfer-case output seal also weeping

before.title: Front Wheel Hub/Bearing Assembly Failure Causing Highway-Speed Humming/Whine (WK2)
before.description: Front wheel hub/bearing assemblies are a recurring wear failure on the WK2 Grand Cherokee, producing a humming, whining, or growling noise that rises with road speed (commonly noticeable from about 35-50 mph) and often changes pitch when the vehicle is loaded or steered left/right. The integrated hub/bearing units wear relatively early, and owners frequently report needing replacement on one or both front corners. Left unaddressed the bearing can develop play and eventually trigger ABS/traction warnings or, in severe cases, lead to hub damage.
before.solution: Confirm the failing corner by listening for the speed-dependent hum and checking for bearing play; the noise typically worsens when turning toward the good side. Replace the affected front hub/bearing assembly (sold as a complete unit). Replacing in pairs is common when both have similar mileage. Verify ABS sensor function after replacement.
symptoms: Humming/whining/growling that increases with speed
Noise changes pitch when turning left or right
Vibration felt through floor/steering at highway speed
Possible ABS or traction-control light if bearing develops play

before.title: 2019 Grand Cherokee ABS Warning - Diagnose the Wheel-Speed Circuit First
before.description: On 2019 model-year Jeep Grand Cherokee (WK) vehicles, an ABS warning that diagnosis traces to a wheel-speed circuit may be caused by an incompletely latched connector, water intrusion and corroded connector pins, rust or contamination at the sensor and tone wheel, or a faulty sensor. FCA warns that replacing a good sensor while leaving a damaged harness in place can cause the concern to return. The previous card incorrectly generalized this condition across 2011-2021 vehicles, named the right-front sensor as a common cause, listed unsupported DTCs and symptoms, and presented three universal repair parts.
before.solution: Read the ABS module and compare individual wheel-speed live data to isolate the affected circuit. Inspect the connector latch, pins, and harness for water intrusion, corrosion, routing problems, or damage; replace a damaged harness rather than the sensor. Inspect and clean the sensor mounting area and tone wheel, reinstall the sensor, and retest the signal. Replace the sensor only when electrical and signal testing confirms it is faulty, then clear faults and verify normal wheel-speed data on a road test. Confirm any replacement by VIN and installed equipment before ordering.
symptoms: ABS warning light illuminated

The corrected scope is 2019 model year only. The prior 2011-2021 range and right-front-specific claim were removed because the reviewed FCA evidence does not establish them.

before.title: Fuel Level Sending Unit Failure Causing Inaccurate Gauge and 'Service Fuel Level Sensor' / P2068 (WK2 Saddle Tank)
before.description: The WK2 uses a saddle-style fuel tank with two fuel-level senders (one per lobe). The sender floats/rheostats stick or wear, and the PCM flags a sender that no longer tracks fuel consumption, setting P2068 (or related P0461/P0463) and a 'Service Fuel Level Sensor' message. Symptoms include a gauge stuck on Full or Empty, wildly bouncing readings, and an inaccurate Distance-to-Empty. It usually doesn't affect running but can strand an owner who trusts a stuck-full gauge, and it commonly requires dropping the tank to access the sender/module.
before.solution: Scan for P2068/P0461/P0463 and confirm which sender is faulty. Inspect the sender for a stuck float and check connector/wiring; some intermittent stuck floats free up, but a failed sender requires replacement of the affected fuel-level sensor/sender module (often the in-tank pump/sender assembly), which typically means lowering the fuel tank. Recalibrate/verify gauge sweep after repair.
symptoms: Fuel gauge stuck on Full or Empty
Gauge reading bounces or drops erratically
'Service Fuel Level Sensor' warning message
Inaccurate Distance-to-Empty / range readout
P2068 or related fuel-level codes
Gauge slow to rise after fill-up

before.title: Heater Core Leak/Clog Causing Sweet Coolant Smell, Foggy Windshield and No Heat
before.description: Grand Cherokees develop heater-core problems from two directions: internal clogging (residual casting sand/scale restricting the fine tubes, producing weak or no heat) and leaks at the core or its plastic firewall inlet/outlet elbows (producing a sweet coolant smell, a greasy fog film on the inside of the windshield, and a damp passenger-side floor). A leaking core also slowly loses coolant and can lead to overheating. The repair is labor-intensive because the dash must be removed to reach the core buried in the HVAC housing, so misdiagnosis is costly.
before.solution: Confirm the diagnosis: sweet smell + foggy windshield + wet passenger carpet = leaking core; cold-only output with good coolant flow points to a clogged core (attempt a back-flush first). Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the plastic heater pipes/elbows at the firewall, which can be replaced separately if that's the leak point. If the core itself leaks or is clogged, replace the heater core (dash-out labor). Refill and bleed the cooling system afterward and verify heat and no coolant loss.
symptoms: Sweet/syrupy coolant smell inside the cabin
Greasy fog film on inside of windshield
Damp or wet front passenger floor carpet
Little or no heat from the vents
Unexplained slow coolant loss

proposal.title: Heater Core Leak/Clog Causing Sweet Coolant Smell, Foggy Windshield and No Heat
proposal.description: Grand Cherokees develop heater-core problems from two directions: internal clogging (residual casting sand/scale restricting the fine tubes, producing weak or no heat) and leaks at the core or its plastic firewall inlet/outlet elbows (producing a sweet coolant smell, a greasy fog film on the inside of the windshield, and a damp passenger-side floor). A leaking core also slowly loses coolant and can lead to overheating. The repair is labor-intensive because the dash must be removed to reach the core buried in the HVAC housing, so misdiagnosis is costly.
proposal.solution: Confirm the diagnosis: sweet smell + foggy windshield + wet passenger carpet = leaking core; cold-only output with good coolant flow points to a clogged core (attempt a back-flush first). Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the plastic heater pipes/elbows at the firewall, which can be replaced separately if that's the leak point. If the core itself leaks or is clogged, replace the heater core (dash-out labor). Refill and bleed the cooling system afterward and verify heat and no coolant loss.
symptoms: Sweet/syrupy coolant smell inside the cabin
Greasy fog film on inside of windshield
Damp or wet front passenger floor carpet
Little or no heat from the vents
Unexplained slow coolant loss
Windows fog and won't clear with defrost

before.title: HID/Xenon Headlight Low-Beam Dimming, Bulb Failure, and Internal Lens Condensation
before.description: Grand Cherokees equipped with factory HID/xenon projector headlights are commonly reported for dim or color-shifted low beams as the bulbs age, single-side bulb or ballast failures, and internal lens condensation. Per Chrysler service guidance, some condensation inside vented HID housings is considered normal and should clear as the bulbs heat up; however, persistent moisture from a failed lens-to-housing seal can corrode reflective surfaces and shorten bulb life. Older assemblies also haze/yellow, further reducing output.
before.solution: For dim/aged output replace the HID bulbs (and ballast if a bulb fails to strike); match bulbs in pairs for even color. For mechanical high/low projector faults inspect the projector shutter solenoid. If condensation does not clear after running the lights, replace the headlight assembly due to a failed seal. Restore hazed lenses or replace assemblies as needed.
symptoms: Dim or yellowed low-beam output
One headlight out or flickering (bulb/ballast)
Fog/condensation inside the headlight lens
High beam not activating on one side
Hazed/yellowed lens reducing brightness

before.title: Hydraulic (Fluid-Filled) Engine Mount Failure Causing Idle Vibration and Clunk (3.6L Pentastar, WK2/WL)
before.description: WK2 (and 5th-gen WL) Grand Cherokees use hydraulic fluid-filled engine mounts. The mounts commonly fail — the internal fluid leaks out (visible reddish-brown residue on the subframe) and the rubber degrades — producing a pronounced vibration felt through the steering wheel, seat, and floor at idle in gear, plus a clunk on acceleration or gear engagement. It is especially prevalent on the 3.6L Pentastar left/front mount, and forums note 2021-2022 units failing repeatedly; a service bulletin exists for the mounts. It is frequently confused with driveline vibration, so both should be checked together.
before.solution: Inspect the engine mounts for fluid weepage and separated rubber; wet/leaking hydraulic mounts should be replaced (replace in pairs on higher-mileage trucks and inspect the transmission mount at the same time). Use OEM Mopar hydraulic mounts rather than solid rubber aftermarket units, which reintroduce vibration. Re-verify idle smoothness in gear after replacement and confirm the driveshaft/mounts aren't jointly contributing.
symptoms: Heavy vibration at idle, worse in Drive/Reverse at a stop
Clunk/thump on acceleration or shifting into gear
Reddish-brown fluid residue on the subframe under the engine
Vibration through steering wheel and floor
Engine 'settling' movement felt in cabin
Repeat failures on newer model years

before.title: Ignition Switch / Lock Cylinder Wear Causing Key Stuck and Unexpected Engine Shut-Off (Recall P41 / NHTSA 14V-438, 2005-2007 WK)
before.description: On 2005-2007 (WK) Grand Cherokees, wear inside the ignition switch/lock cylinder can allow the key to be jarred out of the RUN position — by a knee, a heavy key ring, or a rough road — which shuts off the engine and can disable power steering, power brake assist, and the airbags while driving. Owners also report the key sticking, being hard to turn, or not returning the fob to a working state. FCA issued Safety Recall P41 (NHTSA campaign 14V-438) covering the affected Grand Cherokees; the remedy replaces the ignition switch and lock cylinder assembly. This is a genuine safety defect (unintended stall / loss of assist) rather than a mere inconvenience.
before.solution: Verify the VIN against Safety Recall P41 / NHTSA 14V-438 at a Jeep dealer — the ignition switch and lock cylinder replacement is performed free of charge under the recall. Out of warranty or for non-recalled sticking-key complaints, replace the ignition switch/lock cylinder assembly and inspect the wiring/connector. Interim mitigation: remove heavy items from the key ring so nothing loads the key downward until the repair is done.
symptoms: Engine unexpectedly shuts off while driving
Key can rotate out of RUN with a bump or heavy key ring
Key sticks or is hard to turn in the ignition
Loss of power steering / brake assist after stall
Warning lights or accessories cutting out
Difficulty restarting after the key backs out

before.title: Instrument Cluster Gauge Dropout and Dimming Failure (WJ)
before.description: The WJ-generation Grand Cherokee instrument cluster is a well-known weak point. Owners report gauges that suddenly stop working, read erratically, or dim so far they're unreadable even with the dash brightness turned all the way up. Causes range from loose/corroded cluster connectors and cold-solder joints to electroluminescent backlight aging and Body Control Module (TIPM) interaction. The condition is often intermittent at first (a firm tap on the dash or an odometer-reset press temporarily restores the gauges) before becoming permanent.
before.solution: Remove the cluster and reseat/clean the connectors with contact cleaner; resecure loose plugs. Repair cold-solder joints on the cluster circuit board or replace the cluster (2002-2004 electroluminescent clusters can be retrofitted into 1999-2001 cars). Verify BCM/grounds if multiple unrelated gauges drop together. Re-check connector retention after reinstall.
symptoms: Speedometer/tach/gauges suddenly quit or read erratically
Gauge and odometer backlight too dim to read
Intermittent operation restored by tapping dash or pressing odometer reset
Multiple gauges failing together

before.title: Internal Radiator Transmission-Cooler Failure Cross-Contaminating ATF and Coolant ('Pink Milkshake')
before.description: On the WJ the automatic-transmission fluid cooler is integrated inside the radiator end tank. As the radiator ages the internal cooler barrier fails, allowing engine coolant and ATF to intermix under pressure. The result is a pink/tan 'strawberry milkshake' in both the transmission and cooling system. Coolant (ethylene glycol) in the transmission destroys clutch material and can ruin the 42RE/45RFE if not caught quickly.
before.solution: Stop driving once contamination is found. Replace the radiator (OEM Mopar radiator by application, or aftermarket CSF/Spectra/Koyorad for 1999-2004 WJ) and thoroughly flush the cooling system. Flush/replace ATF and the transmission filter multiple times; badly contaminated transmissions need a rebuild. Many owners add an external auxiliary trans cooler and bypass the in-radiator cooler to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Pink/tan milkshake-colored transmission fluid
Overfilled transmission (rising fluid level)
Discolored or contaminated engine coolant
Harsh shifting, slipping, or limp mode
Coolant loss without external leak

before.title: Loss of Steering Control: Upper Control Arm Pinch Bolt & Intermediate Shaft (Recalls 23V-352, 24V-131)
before.description: On the new WL-generation Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L, two assembly defects can cause loss of steering control. Upper control arm (UCA) pinch bolts damaged during assembly can break and let the UCA separate from the steering knuckle, dropping the wheel outboard. Separately, an incorrectly assembled steering column intermediate shaft can disconnect from the U-joint. Combined recalls cover well over 400,000 vehicles.
before.solution: Have the open recalls performed: NHTSA 23V-352 replaces the steering column intermediate shaft / U-joint assembly, and 24V-131 (with related campaigns) inspects and replaces the upper control arm pinch bolts free of charge. Address any steering play or clunking immediately rather than waiting.
symptoms: Increased free play or looseness in the steering
Clunking or unusual noise when turning
Wandering or imprecise steering
Sudden loss of steering control
Wheel/knuckle separation in severe cases

before.title: Monostable Electronic Shifter Rollaway (Recall 16V-240)
before.description: The 2014-2015 Grand Cherokee uses a ZF monostable electronic 'E-shift' gear selector that always returns to a center position regardless of selected gear, giving poor tactile/visual feedback. NHTSA tied it to over 300 rollaway incidents and 117 crashes after drivers believed they had shifted into Park but had not. FCA recalled 811,586 vehicles (including 2012-2014 Charger/300 with the same shifter) and added Auto Park software.
before.solution: Have the recall (NHTSA 16V-240) performed: dealers install software that automatically applies Park when the driver's door opens with the engine running and the seatbelt unbuckled. The shifter was redesigned to a conventional pattern from MY2016. Until the fix, always confirm the 'P' indicator and set the parking brake before exiting.
symptoms: Vehicle rolls away after the driver believes it is in Park
Difficulty telling which gear is selected from the shifter position
Shifter returns to center after each gear change
Engine left running after exit because shift to Park was not registered

before.title: NV247 Quadra-Trac II / NV242 Transfer Case Fluid Leak, Overheat and Bind/Chatter
before.description: The WJ's on-demand NV247 (Quadra-Trac II) and full-time NV242 (Selec-Trac) transfer cases suffer fluid leaks from the case split-line, rear output slip-yoke seal and a plugged vent, plus a pressure/heat issue: many 1999 units were filled with the WRONG fluid from the factory. Low/incorrect fluid leads to the NV247's progressive coupling binding, chatter on turns and eventual internal wear.
before.solution: Keep the transfer case topped and use the correct fluid — the NV247 requires Mopar/NV247 ATF (equivalent to Mobil 424 hydraulic-tractor fluid), NOT ordinary gear oil. Fix leaks by replacing the rear output/slip-yoke seal and resealing the case halves, and clear/replace the plastic vent cap so pressure can't push fluid past the seals. Verify factory fill on early 1999 units.
symptoms: Fluid leak at the rear output seal or case seam
Low transfer-case fluid
Bind, chatter or hop on tight turns (NV247)
Whine/growl from the transfer case
Fluid pushed out of the vent when hot

proposal.title: NV247 Quadra-Trac II / NV242 Transfer Case Fluid Leak, Overheat and Bind/Chatter
proposal.description: The WJ's on-demand NV247 (Quadra-Trac II) and full-time NV242 (Selec-Trac) transfer cases suffer fluid leaks from the case split-line, rear output slip-yoke seal and a plugged vent, plus a pressure/heat issue: many 1999 units were filled with the WRONG fluid from the factory. before.title: P0171 — System Too Lean (Bank 1) from 3.6L Pentastar Intake Manifold Gasket / Vacuum Leak
before.description: On the WK2 Jeep Grand Cherokee with the 3.6L Pentastar V6, P0171 (and frequently P0174 alongside it) is most commonly triggered by unmetered air entering the engine through a deteriorated intake manifold gasket or a cracked/warped plastic intake manifold. The Pentastar's rubber-and-plastic gaskets become brittle from years of heat cycling and crack, letting in extra air so the upstream O2 sensors report a persistent lean condition. A closely related contributor is the notorious oil filter housing/oil cooler adapter in the engine valley (under the intake manifold) cracking, which is usually addressed at the same time since the intake has to come off. Some early cases are resolved with a PCM software update before parts are replaced.
before.solution: Smoke-test the intake to confirm the vacuum leak, then replace the intake manifold gasket set (and the plastic intake manifold itself if cracked/warped). Because access requires removing the intake, shops commonly replace the leak-prone oil filter housing at the same time. Check for any available PCM software update first, and verify fuel trims return to normal after the repair.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Rough or shaky idle
Hissing/whistling sound from engine bay
Slight loss of power or hesitation
Occasional stalling at idle

before.title: P0442 — Small EVAP Leak from Failed ESIM or Degraded Gas Cap Seal
before.description: P0442 (small EVAP leak, roughly a 0.020–0.040 inch pinhole) is very common on the WK2 Grand Cherokee. The two dominant causes are a degraded gas cap rubber seal and, specific to this platform, a failed Evaporative System Integrity Module (ESIM) mounted in the rear driver-side wheel well. The ESIM is a well-documented WK2 failure point and often fails before other EVAP components; it is known to pass a smoke test yet still set the code because its internal switch fails to report the correct state to the PCM. A vapor canister purge valve stuck slightly open is a secondary cause. There are typically no drivability symptoms beyond the check engine light, and the code can be intermittent (may clear after a few good drive cycles once the cap is tightened).
before.solution: Start with a new OEM Mopar gas cap and confirm it clicks/seals; clear the code and drive several cycles. If it returns, replace the ESIM in the rear driver-side wheel well (accessed behind the fender liner, on the charcoal canister). If still present, smoke-test the EVAP system to find hose/purge-valve/canister leaks.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Intermittent fuel/vapor smell (rare)
No noticeable drivability change
Occasional gas cap warning

before.title: Panoramic (CommandView) Sunroof Spontaneous Shattering / Explosion While Driving
before.description: Owners of panoramic-sunroof-equipped Grand Cherokees (WK2 and 5th-gen WL) report the glass panel spontaneously shattering or 'exploding' with a loud pop while driving on clear days, with no impact. NHTSA complaints and forum reports describe the tempered panel bursting outward/inward, sometimes at low mileage. Suspected causes include factory pre-stress in the tempered glass, ceramic-frit edge stress, thermal cycling, and frame/mechanism stress on the panel. Beyond the repair cost, flying glass and startle-factor while driving make it a safety concern; owners frequently struggle to get warranty coverage and pay out of pocket.
before.solution: There is no preventive repair — the panel must be replaced with new tempered glass (dealer or auto-glass shop), and owners should verify the sunroof frame/track and drains are correct so the replacement isn't re-stressed. Document the event and file an NHTSA complaint (helps trigger any future investigation/coverage) and check comprehensive insurance, which often covers glass with low/no deductible. Retain any FCA/Stellantis goodwill-assistance option for low-mileage vehicles.
symptoms: Loud pop/bang followed by shattered sunroof glass
Spider-cracked or collapsed panoramic panel with no impact
Glass falling into cabin (often caught by sunshade)
Occurs at speed on clear days
Wind noise/water entry after the panel breaks
Sudden startle event while driving

before.title: Parasitic Battery Drain / Ignition-Off Draw Causing Dead Battery and No-Start (5th-Gen WL)
before.description: Owners of 2022-2026 Grand Cherokee and Grand Cherokee L (WL) report severe parasitic battery drain: control modules (infotainment/radio, keyless entry, body modules) fail to enter sleep mode after the vehicle is shut off, rapidly draining the 12V battery. Some report a completely dead battery after the vehicle sits just 7-10 days, with repeated jump-starts and premature battery replacements early in the vehicle's life. The condition can disable safety and convenience features and has prompted a class-action investigation. Chrysler has acknowledged related concerns through TSBs addressing excessive module wake cycles and radio/infotainment-related drain.
before.solution: Have the dealer perform an ignition-off-draw (IOD) parasitic draw test to isolate the offending module, and apply the latest software/TSB updates (e.g., bulletins addressing radio/infotainment module wake cycles). Updating control-module software often reduces the drain. A battery test/replacement may be needed if the original was repeatedly deep-cycled. A battery maintainer helps if the vehicle sits for extended periods.
symptoms: dead battery after sitting a few days
no-start / clicking
repeated jump-starts
warning messages on restart
premature battery replacement
